info.name: Olympus Mobile Server - User APIs (External)
info.description:
Non-superadmin (Public + User Panel) endpoints of the Olympus Mobile Server.
Set serverUrl, clientApiKey and your login credentials in the environment, run 'Login as User' first, then any request.
Admin/superadmin endpoints are intentionally excluded.

request.description: Sends a new one-time password to the signed-in user. Policy `is-logged-in`, so it needs the Bearer token; it takes no input — the recipient is always the caller, and the channel (email / SMS / both) comes from the admin two-factor settings.
Complete a password reset: exchange the emailed `passwordResetToken` (from `recover-password`) for a new password.
Okta/SSO callback verification: validates an externally issued JWT against the client key and mints an Olympus session. Fails with `OKTA_LOGIN_CHANNEL_DISABLED` unless the SSO provider is Okta.

Opens a public folder link. The server checks the link (exists, not expired, mount still allows anonymous folder sharing) and its password, then returns the same token bundle as /entrance/login, signed in as the link's anonymous account. `linkId` is the `accessCode` in the public folder URL; omit `password` for a link without one. This is the only way into an anonymous account — /entrance/login refuses them. Errors: 403 PASSWORD_REQUIRED, 403 INVALID_PASSWORD, 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS (10 wrong per IP / 100 per link per 15 min), 403 LINK_EXPIRED, 400 LINK_INVALID, 400 INVALID_CLIENT.

response.name: Too many attempts
response.body: {"errors":[{"code":"TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS","message":"Too many incorrect password attempts. Please wait 15 minutes and try again."}]}

item.description: Upload-only links into a folder (FE-22). No account, no session: the token in the link is the whole capability.

request.description: Public — no auth. Upload one file through a file-request link. Text fields MUST come before the file part (Skipper). The file is written as the request's creator and never overwrites: a name already taken is stored as "name (1).ext" (the response gives the stored name). Rate limits: 200 uploads per hour per IP, 5000 per day per request (429 TOO_MANY_UPLOADS). Wrong password: 403 INVALID_PASSWORD (attempts limited, then 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS). Audited as FILE_REQUEST_UPLOAD, naming the uploader.

Needs >= READ on the file (LIST is not enough — the overview quotes the content). `canGenerate` = write or admin. No model call.

request.description: Queue overview / key points / tags for an already-indexed file (one utility-model call over its stored summary; no re-embedding). Write access, AI quota pre-flight, at most once per file per minute. 202 queued; 409 NOT_INDEXED; 429 ALREADY_REQUESTED; 400 GENAI_DISABLED. Poll file-ai-details for the result.

Ask a question across everything the caller can access (GENAI-41) — no file or folder id. Sails builds the scope from the caller's permissions (per GenAI-enabled mount: every folder on a wide-access mount, otherwise the folders their permissions reach READ — LIST-only folders are left out, because an answer quotes the documents) and the worker never widens it. Answered asynchronously like the file / folder chats: the row is created `queued`, progress and the streamed answer arrive on the caller's private socket room (subscribe-gen-ai-everything-events), and the stored row carries the answer and its citations. Stored with `entityType: "all"` and `entityId` = the caller. Optional: `selectedModel` (`provider:model`), `chatKnowledgeBase` (`restrictiveToDocuments` · `documentsWithModelKnowledge` · `documentsOrModelKnowledge`), `intent` (`lookup` · `summary` · `comparison`).

request.description:
Small preview of an image file for grid views: a WebP at most 320 px on its longest side, EXIF orientation applied, metadata stripped.

- Access is the same as downloading the file.
- `204 No Content` = no thumbnail for this file (show its type icon): not a JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP/TIFF/AVIF, larger than 50 MB, undecodable, or watermarking is on for its type.
- `ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300`; send `If-None-Match` to get `304`.
- `503` with `Retry-After` when the renderer is saturated.
- Not recorded as a download in the audit log.

**Documents and videos (FE-16).** A PDF, Office document or video is rendered in the background: the first request answers **202** with `Retry-After: 3` (no body) and queues the render; once it is cached the same request answers **200** with a WebP (ETag / 304 as for images), or **204** when it could not be rendered (not retried until the file changes). A PDF answers 204 while watermarking is on, like other watermarked types.

request.description:
Which parts does the server already hold? This is the resume handshake.

Call it before retrying, then send only the missing indices. The received set is read from disk, so it can never claim a part the server does not actually have.

A 404 (UPLOAD_SESSION_NOT_FOUND) means the session expired or was cleaned up — start again from upload-init.

Lock a file so nobody else can rename, move, delete or overwrite it until it is unlocked (needs write or admin on the file). Locking a file you already hold is a no-op; a file locked by someone else answers 423 FILE_LOCKED with lockedBy / lockedByName / lockedAt. Locks do not expire. Broadcasts FILE_LOCK_CHANGE to the folder's room.

request.description: Release a lock. Allowed for the holder, a file admin (a forced unlock — `forced: true`, audited as FILE_UNLOCK) or a super-admin; a system lock (lockedBy -1) only by a super-admin. Anyone else gets 403 NOT_LOCK_HOLDER; 409 LOCK_CHANGED if the lock changed hands mid-request. Unlocking an unlocked file is a no-op.

request.description:
Send one part. multipart/form-data with `chunkIndex` and a single file field `chunk`.

IMPORTANT — append `chunkIndex` BEFORE the file. The server parses text fields as they stream, so one arriving after the file part is not visible to it.

`chunkIndex` is in the BODY rather than the query string on purpose: a CORS preflight is cached per URL, so a per-chunk query parameter makes every part pay a fresh OPTIONS round trip. Keeping the URL constant across a session means browsers preflight once.

Parts are ADDRESSED, not appended — `chunkIndex` says which slice this is. They may be sent in any order AND SEVERAL AT ONCE (3 concurrent is a good default), and re-sending one that already arrived is a successful no-op. That is what makes retrying safe when you cannot tell whether your request was lost or only its response.

Slice boundaries: bytes `[chunkIndex * chunkSize, min((chunkIndex+1) * chunkSize, totalSize))`. Every part is exactly `chunkSize` except the last.

`chunkSha256` may be sent as an extra form field; a mismatch is reported as CHUNK_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH and is safe to retry.

Assemble the parts and create the file. Returns the same envelope as /file/upload.

Refuses with UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE (listing the missing indices) if any part is absent, and with UPLOAD_SIZE_MISMATCH if the assembled size does not match what was declared.

Safe to call again if the response was lost: a completed session replays the same result instead of re-creating the file or re-running indexing. Do NOT call it concurrently — a second caller receives 409 UPLOAD_IN_PROGRESS.

Open a resumable upload session for a large file.

Use this instead of /file/upload when the file is bigger than ~10 MB: the transfer is split into parts, so a dropped connection costs one part instead of the whole file.

`directoryId` MUST stay in the query string — the permission policy reads it before the body is parsed.

`totalSize` is validated against the mount's file-size cap and the guest storage quota up front, so an upload that cannot succeed is refused before any bytes move.

Returns the server-chosen `chunkSize` — always use the returned value, and reuse it when resuming.

request.description: Confirm or cancel a destructive tool call the in-app MCP agent is holding (MCP-32). When the model asks for a tool the server marks `destructiveHint` (delete, share, make public, remove…) it is not run: the exact call is stored for 30 min and the assistant message carries an action card (`metaData.actions`: id, tool, summary, status). Only the same user, on the same chat, can decide; `confirm` runs the STORED arguments — what runs is what was shown — and the card's status moves to running → done / failed; `cancel` drops it. The outcome arrives on the MCP chat socket room. `actionId` is the card's 16-character id; `messageId` the assistant message it hangs off. 404 for an unknown message or action; an expired or already-decided action is refused.

Revoke one directory share by its `SharedItems` id — works on any user's share, which is the point of the admin variant. The recipient loses what this share gave on the folder at once and on everything under it shortly after; another person's share of the same folder with the same user is untouched.

Revoke one file share by its `SharedItems` id — works on any user's share, which is the point of the admin variant. Public links stop resolving immediately. Only this share's access is taken back; another person's share of the same file with the same user is untouched.
Your file request for a folder (one per user per folder), or null. Needs write or admin on the folder. The password is never returned — only passwordProtected.

request.description: Create or update your upload-only link into a folder (FE-22). `enabled: false` deletes it (its link stops working; turning it on again issues a new link). The mount must allow anonymous folder sharing (403 ANONYMOUS_DIRECTORY_SHARING_DISABLED / DIRECTORY_SHARING_DISABLED otherwise); a mount's top-level folder is refused (NOT_SHARABLE). Password: at least 6 characters with a letter and a digit, stored as a bcrypt hash; a blank password keeps the existing one. expiryDate is an ISO instant in the future.
